alert: Ariva stored secrets under Data Protection keys no signer signed (${environment})
description: The upgrade check of ARV-211 (every API host at start, Cronz's KeyLifecycle job every day) found stored values (user TOTP seeds, integration client seeds, outbound secrets) that need a Data Protection key the hosts refuse, in an installation already upgraded or while DataProtection:Signing:RetiredSignerAcceptedUntil accepts the loss of a signer's keys, by outcome. Only keys the hosts refuse now count, so an upgrade with its window open raises nothing. unsigned: a key without a row signature (written before ARV-211): the window DataProtection:Signing:CertificateSignedUntil was closed before SecretReprotection moved them, a value it could not move, or a row a database writer added. retired-signer: a key signed by a key ring signing certificate no host has configured: a rotation's previous signer removed before SecretReprotection moved them, which only configuring that signer again (dataProtectionSigningPreviousSecretName) fixes, or a signing certificate lost for good, whose values are set again (runbook section 4.13); the window does not admit these keys. Those values no longer unprotect, so those users cannot sign in with their authenticator and those clients and endpoints fail; the hosts start nonetheless.

annotations.summary: Stored secrets under keys the hosts refuse: {{$outcome}}
annotations.description: {{$value}} stored values need a Data Protection key the hosts refuse ({{$outcome}}), held for ${keyRingUnsigned.minutes} minutes. unsigned: if SecretReprotection has not run since the upgrade, reopen the window and run it. retired-signer: if it has not run since the signing rotation, configure the previous signer again (dataProtectionSigningPreviousSecretName) and run it; if that certificate is lost for good, have the values set again (runbook section 4.13). Otherwise find the rows it named as not re-protected and have them set again, and treat a key row no host wrote as a database writer's work.
